name: Amber White
lede: Amber White is a pale, warm cream from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, and in our archive it almost always plays the highlight.

sections.title: A cream from one dictionary
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary records Amber White, plate 11 C 1, first recorded in 1500 [1]. No other system in our library carries the name, and who first used it beyond that 1500 record is undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[glass-green]], [[lion]], [[baryta-yellow]] and [[lemon-meringue]], at 2.8, 2.8, 3.5 and 3.8 ΔE [1]. Among pale yellows it sits beside [[amber]] and [[tan]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this cream in 802 of 23,781 paintings, 3.4 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is a page from a copy of the Qur'an, dated 799 in our archive, seven centuries before the name's 1500 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. It peaks in the 1840s, in 46 of 699 paintings, at 1.95 times the archive's overall rate, and Pieter Gerardus van Os carries it in four of his 13 paintings here [2]. Inside a painting it is overwhelmingly a highlight, in 98 percent of its appearances [2].
